Part 2&3 事件 EVENTS AI 补全经历

Describe a time when you gave advice to others

描述一次你给别人建议的经历

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a time when you gave advice to others

  • When it was (是什么时候)
  • To whom you gave the advice (你给谁建议)
  • What the advice was (你给的是什么建议)
  • And explain why you gave the advice (并解释你为什么给建议)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a time when you gave advice to others

I'd like to talk about a time when I gave advice to a classmate about learning programming. This happened during my second year at university, when I was already studying computer science. The person I gave advice to was a classmate of mine, a guy who shared a few courses with me. He'd been thinking about learning to code for a while, but he kept putting it off because he didn't know where to start. One day he came up to me after class and asked which programming language he should begin with. The advice I gave him was to start with Python. I told him that Python has a very simple and readable syntax, which makes it much easier for beginners to pick up. I also mentioned that there are tons of free resources online, like tutorials and practice websites, so he wouldn't have to spend any money. Most importantly, I said that starting with an easy language means you're less likely to give up in the first few weeks, which is exactly when most people quit. The reason I gave this advice is that I'd been through the same struggle myself. When I first started, I tried a difficult language and almost gave up, so I knew from experience how important it is to build confidence early. He listened to my suggestion, and a few months later he told me he could already write small tools with Python. I felt genuinely happy that my advice had helped him get started.

讲的是大二时给一个同学学编程的建议。给谁：一个同班同学，想学编程但一直拖着，不知道从哪开始，课后问我该先学哪门语言。什么建议：建议他从 Python 入手，语法简单易读，新手容易上手；网上免费资源多，不用花钱；最重要的是从简单的语言开始，头几周不容易放弃，而大多数人正是在这时候放弃的。为什么给：我自己踩过同样的坑，一开始学了门难的语言差点放弃，所以知道早期建立信心有多重要。结果：他听了建议，几个月后说已经能用 Python 写小工具了，我很开心建议帮到了他。

Q2Should people prepare before giving advice?

Yes, I think people should prepare before giving advice, especially when the topic is serious. If you give advice without understanding the person's situation, it can easily be misleading or even harmful. For example, when someone asks about career choices, you need to know their background and interests first. That said, for small everyday matters, a quick and honest opinion is usually fine. So I'd say preparation matters more when the stakes are higher.

是的，给建议前应该准备，尤其是严肃话题。不了解对方情况就建议容易误导甚至有害，比如职业选择要先了解背景和兴趣。不过日常小事随口给个诚实意见就行。事情越重要越需要准备。

Q3Is it good to ask advice from strangers online?

I think it can be helpful in some ways, but it also has risks. Online, you can get a wide range of opinions from people with different experiences, which is useful for things like choosing a phone or planning a trip. However, strangers don't know your personal situation, and some advice online is simply wrong or even dangerous, especially about health or money. So I'd say it's fine for general questions, but for important decisions, you should rely on people you trust.

网上问陌生人建议有好处也有风险。好处是能听到各种不同经验的人的意见，适合选手机、规划旅行这类事；但陌生人不知道你的个人情况，网上有些建议是错的甚至危险的，尤其是健康和钱的事。一般问题可以问，重要决定要靠信任的人。

Q4What are the personalities of people whose job is to give advice to others?

I think people who give advice professionally, like consultants or career counsellors, usually share some common traits. They tend to be patient and good listeners, because they need to understand the problem fully before saying anything. They're also quite analytical, since they have to weigh different options and explain them clearly. On top of that, they need to be empathetic, because people often come to them when they're worried or confused. So I'd say listening skills and empathy are probably the most important qualities.

以给建议为职业的人，比如顾问、职业咨询师，通常有共同特质：耐心、善于倾听，因为要先完全理解问题才能开口；分析能力强，要权衡各种选项并解释清楚；还要有同理心，因为人们往往在焦虑困惑时来找他们。倾听和同理心最重要。

Q5What are the problems if you ask too many people for advice?

The main problem is that you end up with too many conflicting opinions, which makes it harder to decide, not easier. Different people will give different suggestions based on their own experiences, and some of them will contradict each other. As a result, you might spend so much time comparing opinions that you never actually make a move. I think it's better to ask one or two people you trust, and then make your own decision, because in the end, you're the one who has to live with it.

主要问题是会得到太多互相矛盾的意见，反而更难决定。不同人基于自己的经验给不同建议，有些还互相冲突，结果你可能花大量时间比较意见，最后根本没行动。最好问一两个信任的人，然后自己做决定，因为最终承担后果的是你自己。

Q6Why do some people think it is better to ask for advice from friends than from parents?

I think it's mainly because friends are closer to your own age and situation, which makes their advice feel more relevant. Parents, on the other hand, grew up in a different era, and their suggestions can sometimes feel out of touch with modern life. Friends also understand your daily struggles better, and they're less likely to judge you. That said, parents usually have more life experience, so I think the ideal approach is to listen to both and take what makes sense.

主要是因为朋友年龄和处境更接近，建议更贴合实际；父母成长于不同年代，建议有时显得跟不上现代生活。朋友也更懂你日常的难处，更不会评判你。不过父母人生经验更多，理想做法是两边都听，取有用的部分。

Q7When would old people ask young people for advice?

Old people would usually ask young people for advice about technology and modern trends. For example, many older people ask their children or grandchildren how to use smartphones, pay online, or set up video calls. They might also ask about new things like social media or electric cars, which they didn't grow up with. I think this is a natural exchange, because young people are more familiar with the digital world, while older people have more experience in other areas of life.

老人通常向年轻人请教科技和现代潮流方面的事。比如很多老人问子女或孙辈怎么用智能手机、在线支付、开视频通话；也会问社交媒体、电动车这类他们没经历过的新事物。这是自然的互补，年轻人更熟悉数字世界，老人则在生活其他方面经验更多。
